source_part_identity: p0-p27 preserve exact catalog/cache identities; semantic a_* ids identify added parts without assuming native order. Every name resolves uniquely to a ModelDataset item index.

sources.title: University of Leeds: epidermal layers
sources.supports: Basal division, desmosome-linked spinous cells, granular differentiation, flattened terminal squames and shedding.

sources.title: University of Minnesota Histology Guide: MH 090 human thin skin
sources.supports: Four thin-skin strata; basal attachment, spinosum contacts, granular cells and anucleate corneum.

sources.title: University of Leeds: epidermal cells
sources.supports: Basal melanocyte bodies with intercellular processes; concentric Pacinian capsule around afferent ending.

sources.title: Crawford et al.: Integrin-linked kinase regulates melanosome trafficking and melanin transfer
sources.supports: Primary experimental support for maturation, trafficking to dendritic tips, dendricity and transfer to neighboring keratinocytes; not proof of one exclusive in-vivo transfer route.

sources.title: University of Leeds: epithelial glands
sources.supports: Sebocyte lipid accumulation and holocrine disintegration, short duct into hair canal; simple secretory epithelium versus two-layer cuboidal eccrine duct, pore and evaporation.

sources.title: University of Minnesota Histology Guide: MH 086b scalp
sources.supports: Hair cortex/cuticle, inner sheath height, outer sheath continuity, sebaceous secretion into follicle, eccrine compartments and attached arrector pili.

sources.title: NCBI Bookshelf: Physiology, Hair
sources.supports: Matrix production, papilla signaling/nutrition, anagen growth, catagen regression and telogen quiescence; cycle regulation is incompletely known.

sources.title: Reddy and Quinton: Functional interaction of CFTR and ENaC in sweat glands
sources.supports: Native human sweat-duct experiments: CFTR and ENaC support parallel NaCl absorption; CFTR loss reduces ductal salt absorption. Do not import airway ENaC behavior into sweat duct.

sources.title: University of Leeds: skin layers and circulation
sources.supports: Dermal blood supply supports avascular epidermis; deep plexus supplies appendages/fat and subpapillary plexus supplies papillary loops.

sources.title: Pawson et al.: GABAergic/glutamatergic glial-neuronal interaction contributes to rapid adaptation
sources.supports: Experimental rapidly adapting Pacinian responses; capsule-associated mechanochemical contribution, so adaptation must not be claimed exclusively mechanical. Cat mesenteric receptor experiments are not scalp density evidence.

sources.title: NCBI Bookshelf: Anatomy, Head and Neck, Scalp
sources.supports: Skin/subcutaneous tissue firmly bound to galea; loose tissue and pericranium below; neurovascular structures in connective tissue and top layers move as a unit.

sources.title: Buono et al.: Heat acclimation causes a linear decrease in sweat sodium ion concentration
sources.supports: Four-participant human study: sweat sodium concentration changed at a given sweat rate after heat acclimation. Supports a qualitative limitation against fixed displayed salt concentration; not scalp-specific calibration.

sources.title: Baker and Wolfe: Physiological mechanisms determining eccrine sweat composition
sources.supports: Published review abstract identifies secretion/reabsorption, sweat flow, gland metabolism, skin contamination and collection methods as influences on final sweat composition. Supporting context, not primary source or a model measurement.

application.call: apply_stage_to_view(model_view, sequence_id, stage_id, anchors, available_geometry=(), require_verified_geometry=True)

application.scope: Source-only controller; the lead supplies an immutable cache-backed review entry. This does not install, launch or alter the original application.
application.section_coordinates: Authored common-settle-warped model coordinates pass unchanged to ProceduralModel. No dataset normalization exists in this route. Section index 0 sagittal X, 1 coronal Z, 2 transverse Y.
application.visible_detail: Host-matched split nuclei and tissue fibers are explicit selectors; relational connective support stays ghosted. Missing names fail before mutation.
application.animation_contract: All overlays remain off. No route payload, per-vertex phase or cycle geometry has been supplied. Existing native modes are a future format, not an enabled biological simulation.
application.session_contract: capture_stage_session/restore_stage_session preserve all controller-mutated native state. Camera is untouched by this adapter; host teaching camera changes require separate restoration.
application.inspection: require_verified_geometry=False permits static source-stage inspection and returns missing capabilities; never constitutes anatomical approval.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Basal progenitors replenish cohesive suprabasal layers; differentiating cells flatten, establish the surface barrier and desquamate.

steps.title: Start at the dermoepidermal junction
steps.caption: Basal cells remain attached at the junction while selected daughter cells enter the suprabasal population.
steps.acceptance: Anatomical readiness requires saved geometry and visual section review; a successful stage-control call proves only state selection.

steps.title: Trace a cohesive cell column
steps.caption: Polygonal keratinocytes retain intercellular junctions as the population differentiates. Prickles in routine slides reflect fixation around desmosomal contacts.
steps.acceptance: Anatomical readiness requires saved geometry and visual section review; a successful stage-control call proves only state selection.

steps.title: Inspect the granular-to-cornified transition
steps.caption: Granular differentiation precedes anucleate, flattened surface squames. Show structural granules and intercellular barrier organization in the same column.
steps.acceptance: Anatomical readiness requires saved geometry and visual section review; a successful stage-control call proves only state selection.

steps.title: Follow surface replacement
steps.caption: The uppermost squames are shed; layer stacks remain continuous. Stage advance is an educational sequence, not a live cell tracked through weeks.
steps.acceptance: Anatomical readiness requires saved geometry and visual section review; a successful stage-control call proves only state selection.

schematic_limitations: Do not animate entire sheets translating upward or explode layers to imply physiological gaps.
Cell counts, keratin bundles and lipid lamellae are enlarged selected samples, not measured cell density.
Molecular keratin/filaggrin pathways and precise turnover time are not simulated.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Melanocytes produce pigment-bearing organelles and distribute pigment through dendritic relationships to adjacent epidermal keratinocytes.

steps.title: Locate cell body and dendrites
steps.caption: Keep the basal cell body and recipient keratinocytes together in view.
steps.acceptance: Anatomical readiness requires saved geometry and visual section review; a successful stage-control call proves only state selection.

steps.title: Trace pigment transfer
steps.caption: Pigment travels toward dendritic tips and reaches neighboring keratinocytes. Transfer is displayed schematically without choosing one exclusive membrane mechanism.
steps.acceptance: Anatomical readiness requires saved geometry and visual section review; a successful stage-control call proves only state selection.

steps.title: Inspect recipient pigment distribution
steps.caption: Static pigment caps are selected over basal recipient nuclei. This sampled distribution supports cell-scale UV protection teaching; it is not a measured transfer trajectory or whole-skin phototype prediction.
steps.acceptance: Anatomical readiness requires saved geometry and visual section review; a successful stage-control call proves only state selection.

schematic_limitations: Existing p4 represents epidermal melanocytes; do not use it as a hair-bulb melanocyte population.
Transfer route arrows or particles are an instructional abstraction; molecular membrane exchange remains debated.
No programmed change in whole skin color or racial phototype claims.

functional_sequences.mechanism: The anagen matrix around the dermal papilla produces the shaft and inner root sheath while the outer sheath remains a continuous epithelial host.

steps.title: Identify a production unit
steps.caption: Terminal bulb reaches subcutaneous tissue; gland and muscle attachment belong to the selected follicular unit.
steps.acceptance: Anatomical readiness requires saved geometry and visual section review; a successful stage-control call proves only state selection.

steps.title: Inspect papilla embraced by matrix
steps.caption: Distinguish connective papilla from a proliferative epithelial cup. The papilla is a tissue component with a vascular supply, not a hollow feed tube.
steps.acceptance: Anatomical readiness requires saved geometry and visual section review; a successful stage-control call proves only state selection.

steps.title: Compare shaft and sheath products
steps.caption: Matrix-derived cells mature into the hair and guiding inner sheath; inner sheath ends near the sebaceous outlet while outer sheath continues.
steps.acceptance: Anatomical readiness requires saved geometry and visual section review; a successful stage-control call proves only state selection.

steps.title: Compare layers in a transverse section
steps.caption: Inspect cellular sheaths and shaft architecture at one documented level; upper and lower follicle levels differ.
steps.acceptance: Anatomical readiness requires saved geometry and visual section review; a successful stage-control call proves only state selection.

schematic_limitations: Static specimen is anagen. Shaft elongation is not a rigid translation of the complete follicle.
Medulla is variable; do not require every terminal shaft to have a continuous central cavity.
Basal epidermal melanocyte p4 does not explain follicular pigmentation; a dedicated bulb pigment population is additional geometry, not relabeling.

functional_sequences.mechanism: A permanent upper follicle is retained while its lower epithelial growth apparatus cycles through growth, regression and rest.

steps.title: Inspect the anagen reference
steps.caption: This tissue geometry is the anagen reference. Cycle stages below are a narrated structural comparison and require a separate authored inset to show remodeling.
steps.acceptance: Anatomical readiness requires saved geometry and visual section review; a successful stage-control call proves only state selection.

steps.title: Discuss lower-segment regression
steps.caption: Catagen ceases matrix production and regresses the lower epithelium; the permanent upper follicle persists. Reference meshes remain anagen.
steps.acceptance: Anatomical readiness requires saved geometry and visual section review; a successful stage-control call proves only state selection.

steps.title: Discuss rest and club hair retention
steps.caption: Telogen has no active shaft production; club-hair retention and later shedding differ from active growth. Reference meshes remain anagen.
steps.acceptance: Anatomical readiness requires saved geometry and visual section review; a successful stage-control call proves only state selection.

steps.title: Relate regeneration to the permanent follicle
steps.caption: Regeneration restores the lower growth apparatus through epithelial–mesenchymal interactions. Stage timing and signal networks are simplified.
steps.acceptance: Anatomical readiness requires saved geometry and visual section review; a successful stage-control call proves only state selection.

schematic_limitations: No native cycle deformation exists in the selected baseline. Controls expose the anagen reference; captions never claim it is catagen/telogen geometry.
A future inset needs separately authored phase geometry; topology loss and club formation cannot be truthfully encoded as uniform scaling.
The three displayed follicles are sampled anatomy, not synchronized cycle statistics.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Peripheral sebaceous cells mature inward, accumulate lipid and disintegrate; sebum exits via the short duct into the follicular canal.

steps.title: Identify lobule, outlet and host
steps.caption: Trace the outlet into the upper follicle; do not present a blind gland next to a hair.
steps.acceptance: Anatomical readiness requires saved geometry and visual section review; a successful stage-control call proves only state selection.

steps.title: Inspect the secretory gradient
steps.caption: Follow the separately selectable peripheral, maturing and terminal-breakdown sebocyte samples toward the gland duct. Lipid accumulation and holocrine disintegration are represented as a spatial maturation comparison, not a tracked cell or measured secretion rate.
steps.acceptance: Anatomical readiness requires saved geometry and visual section review; a successful stage-control call proves only state selection.

steps.title: Follow product to the follicular canal
steps.caption: Sebum includes cell-derived lipid and debris. Any payload follows the authored duct/follicular route.
steps.acceptance: Anatomical readiness requires saved geometry and visual section review; a successful stage-control call proves only state selection.

steps.title: Inspect attachment relationships
steps.caption: The arrector pili attaches at the follicular bulge and superficial dermis. Do not move an unsupported strap away from both attachment sites.
steps.acceptance: Anatomical readiness requires saved geometry and visual section review; a successful stage-control call proves only state selection.

schematic_limitations: Holocrine disintegration is distinct from exocytosis; whole-gland collapse is not the mechanism.
Duct outlet label is the upper follicular canal near the isthmus/infundibulum boundary, not deep bulb or separate surface sweat pore.
Muscle contraction is not required for basal sebaceous secretion.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Eccrine secretory epithelium generates primary fluid, the duct reabsorbs salt, and a separate surface pore enables evaporative cooling.

steps.title: Inspect secretory coil
steps.caption: Simple secretory epithelium and supporting myoepithelial relationships border the coil lumen.
steps.acceptance: Anatomical readiness requires saved geometry and visual section review; a successful stage-control call proves only state selection.

steps.title: Compare the duct wall
steps.caption: A two-layer cuboidal duct reabsorbs NaCl with relatively little accompanying water; final sweat is generally hypotonic. Salt concentration varies with sweat flow and transport capacity, neither of which this model measures.
steps.acceptance: Anatomical readiness requires saved geometry and visual section review; a successful stage-control call proves only state selection.

steps.title: Trace the surface passage
steps.caption: The epidermal passage opens at its own sweat pore. Sweat remains separate from the sebaceous follicular outlet; evaporation cools the surface.
steps.acceptance: Anatomical readiness requires saved geometry and visual section review; a successful stage-control call proves only state selection.

schematic_limitations: Native duct channel experiments support transport direction, not rendered channel density.
Na+ and Cl− arrows are separate educational vectors from duct lumen across epithelium; do not send whole water stream through the wall.
No gland-pressure, electrolyte concentration, transport-rate or sweat-test prediction; reduced CFTR function is an optional qualitative comparison only.
Mesh cell tiles and nuclei cannot establish clear/dark secretory cell phenotype or transporter localization. Sweat flow and electrolyte composition are not computed.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Deep supply feeds appendages and superficial branches; capillary exchange supports living skin, and superficial/deep venous routes collect drainage.

steps.title: Locate supply and drainage in tissue
steps.caption: Deep routes occupy connective tissue; fine branches must visibly supply the selected deep appendages.
steps.acceptance: Anatomical readiness requires saved geometry and visual section review; a successful stage-control call proves only state selection.

steps.title: Inspect deep appendage supply
steps.caption: Inspect tissue-bounded capillary relationships around the bulb, papilla and gland before enabling any flow cue.
steps.acceptance: Anatomical readiness requires saved geometry and visual section review; a successful stage-control call proves only state selection.

steps.title: Trace papillary exchange beneath the epidermis
steps.caption: Papillary loops remain dermal; living epidermis receives diffusible nutrients without blood vessels entering it.
steps.acceptance: Anatomical readiness requires saved geometry and visual section review; a successful stage-control call proves only state selection.

steps.title: Follow the return route
steps.caption: Distinguish arterial delivery and venous collection within the mixed subpapillary part. Colors encode schematic route identity rather than an abrupt oxygenation transition.
steps.acceptance: Anatomical readiness requires saved geometry and visual section review; a successful stage-control call proves only state selection.

schematic_limitations: p19–p22 baseline are solid course illustrations; they do not establish hollow lumen walls or CFD-ready networks.
Combined p21 cannot receive one uniform flow direction: arterial/venous subcourses need independent per-vertex phases or separate payloads.
Exchange does not mean red cells entering epidermis or gland lumen. No scalp arterial territory map, hemodynamics, thermoregulatory shunt density or emissary vein model.
Appendage exchange capillaries is a distinct selectable course illustration; Papillary capillary loops remains the superficial selector. Neither supplies hollow vessel walls or measured blood flow.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Distinct endings preserve target relationships and convey sensory information along cutaneous afferents.

steps.title: Inspect endings against the follicle
steps.caption: Hair deflection strains follicle-associated mechanosensory endings. The outer sheath and its nuclei remain ghosted as targets; the retained ending course is a representative arrangement, not human scalp subtype or density evidence.
steps.acceptance: Anatomical readiness requires saved geometry and visual section review; a successful stage-control call proves only state selection.

steps.title: Inspect epithelial free endings
steps.caption: Free endings enter or approach their target tissue; pain/thermal/itch modalities are not inferred solely from a twig shape.
steps.acceptance: Anatomical readiness requires saved geometry and visual section review; a successful stage-control call proves only state selection.

steps.title: Inspect lamellae and central terminal
steps.caption: The central terminal is enveloped by lamellae and fluid/interstitial spaces. This enlarged receptor example does not assert typical scalp abundance.
steps.acceptance: Anatomical readiness requires saved geometry and visual section review; a successful stage-control call proves only state selection.

steps.title: Relate target to nerve course
steps.caption: Sensory cues travel from the target toward the cutaneous nerve. Autonomic cues to glands, arterioles and muscle use a separate mode and opposite teaching direction.
steps.acceptance: Anatomical readiness requires saved geometry and visual section review; a successful stage-control call proves only state selection.

schematic_limitations: Pacinian rapid adaptation should not be described as exclusively mechanical filtering; experimental glial-neuronal contributions exist.
No simulated action-potential velocity, threshold, receptor density, firing rate or universal adaptation profile for every follicular ending.
Rodent lanceolate microstructure is useful comparative evidence, not exact human scalp subtype mapping.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Dense subcutaneous connective septa bind skin and fat compartments to galea; deeper scalp layers continue below the specimen boundary.

steps.title: Identify the connected upper scalp unit
steps.caption: The block includes skin, dense subcutaneous connective tissue and galea, with deep follicular bulbs among fat compartments.
steps.acceptance: Anatomical readiness requires saved geometry and visual section review; a successful stage-control call proves only state selection.

steps.title: Inspect the septal attachment path
steps.caption: Hide fat only after ghosting preserves its compartment boundaries. Septa connect the overlying tissue to the galea and carry neurovascular routes.
steps.acceptance: Anatomical readiness requires saved geometry and visual section review; a successful stage-control call proves only state selection.

steps.title: Inspect the galeal undersurface
steps.caption: The specimen ends at the galea. Loose areolar tissue, pericranium and calvarium continue below and are outside this model; a base sheet alone is insufficient tissue explanation.
steps.acceptance: Anatomical readiness requires saved geometry and visual section review; a successful stage-control call proves only state selection.

schematic_limitations: Do not independently slide skin across its septa/galea attachments to imply normal mobility.
A future motion inset must move the upper tissue unit together over an explicitly external loose-plane reference.
The model does not include skull, subgaleal space, pericranium, occipitofrontalis or emissary routes; clinical spread/gaping requires additional anatomy.
